statement.p: Does the function f(x,y) = \frac{x^{2}}{2}+3y^{3}+3y^{2}-7x have a global maximum and global minimum? If it does, identify the value of the maximum and minimum. If it does not, be sure that you are able to explain why.

p.em: (Enter the value of the global maximum, or none if there is no global maximum.)
(Enter the value of the global minimum, or none if there is no global minimum.)

static.solution: x is fixed. Then for large values of y the sign of f is determined by the highest power of y, namely y^3. Thus, f(x,y)\to\infty as y\to\infty, and there can be no global maximum. For y\to-\infty we similarly have f(x,y)\to-\infty, so that there is no global minimum either.
